name: /slashforge-code

Pass `-quick` for lean mode on small changes (skips brainstorming, minimal plan, inline self-review instead of the agent review). Uses SlashForge's own skills at each phase — no plugins required.

name: /slashforge-debug
description: Find the root cause before proposing any fix. Use for any bug, test failure, or unexpected behaviour — especially when the fix looks obvious or time is short. Requires a reproduction and a failing regression test before code changes.

name: /slashforge-fix
description: Fix a bug straight from a `/slashforge-investigate` finding — reads `.slashforge/latest_investigation.json`, locks context to the implicated files, writes a regression test first, then patches. The tight investigate → code loop, with no full-feature planning phase.

name: /slashforge-investigate
description: Research-only flow — reproduce and root-cause a bug or suspected issue. Produces a findings report. No branch, no PR, no code changes.

name: /slashforge-parallel
description: Execute an approved plan by dispatching one agent per task, reviewing between each. Use only when the plan has two or more genuinely independent units — tasks that share no state and no ordering.

name: /slashforge-plan
description: Turn an approved spec into a step-by-step implementation plan. Use after a design is agreed and before touching code. Produces bite-sized tasks with real code, real commands, and no placeholders.

name: /slashforge-refactor
description: Refactor code with a zero-functional-change guarantee — gated by the existing test suite passing with identical results before and after. Structure only: no behaviour, API, or feature changes.

name: /slashforge-request-review
description: Get your own work reviewed before it goes out — by a fresh reviewer with crafted context, not your session history. Use after implementing, before pushing or opening a PR.

name: /slashforge-resume
description: Resume an interrupted /slashforge-code or /slashforge-fix run from its last checkpoint — reads `.slashforge/run_<id>.ckpt.json`, verifies the git HEAD still matches, and re-enters the workflow at the next phase instead of starting over.

name: /slashforge-review-feedback
description: Evaluate code review feedback technically before implementing any of it. Use when receiving review comments, especially if a suggestion seems unclear or wrong — requires verification and reasoned pushback, not agreement.

name: /slashforge-review-pr
description: Review a pull request against this repo's own rules and conventions, then post line-level comments or approve — only after you confirm. Lists PRs awaiting your review; pass --assigned, --mine or --all to change what it looks for.

name: /slashforge-setup

name: /slashforge-tdd

name: /slashforge-test

name: /slashforge-verify

Use when the user wants to close the books for a period starting from the transactions and source documents. Not for logging day-to-day transactions as they happen; see /bookkeeping-record.

name: accounting-audit
description: Audit specific accounts or transactions — vouching, tracing, recalculation, confirmation and analytical procedures — with each finding's cause, effect and fix. Use when the user suspects a balance is wrong or wants an account tested against its supporting documents. Not for explaining the gap between one account and its statement; see /accounting-reconciliation.

name: accounting-close
description: Close revenue, expense and dividend accounts to retained earnings and prepare the post-closing trial balance that opens the next period. Use when the user has the period's financial statements done and wants the temporary accounts zeroed and balances rolled forward. Not for starting a period's close from source documents; see /accounting-analyze.

name: accounting-controls
description: Design internal controls — segregation of duties, approvals, reconciliations, reviews — mapped to the entity's error and fraud risks in a control matrix with owners. Use when the user worries about errors or fraud in cash, payroll or reporting and wants controls to prevent or catch them. Not for assessing SOX, FINRA or SEC compliance; see /compliance-financial-compliance.

name: accounting-journal
description: Record numbered double-entry journal entries from the analyzed transaction register, each with balanced debits and credits. Use when the user has a transaction register for a period and asks to journalize it or book the transactions. Not for sorting everyday bank lines into accounts, or posting entries to ledger accounts; see /bookkeeping-categorize or /accounting-ledger.

name: accounting-ledger
description: Post journal entries to the general ledger by account, with running balances, closing balances and a journal-to-ledger cross-reference. Use when the user has a period's journal entries and wants them posted to ledger accounts or needs each account's balance. Not for writing the journal entries themselves; see /accounting-journal.

name: accounting-materiality
description: Determine overall, performance and trivial materiality thresholds from a chosen benchmark plus qualitative factors, and apply them to known misstatements as adjust or pass. Use when the user asks whether a misstatement is big enough to fix or disclose, or needs a materiality level for an audit or close.

name: accounting-reconciliation
description: Reconcile one ledger account to its bank, customer or vendor statement or sub-ledger, explaining every difference and listing the correcting entries. Use when an account's book balance does not agree with an outside statement or sub-ledger and the user needs the gap explained. Not for matching a whole period of bookkeeping entries to statements; see /bookkeeping-reconcile.

name: accounting-statements
description: Prepare the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement with notes from an adjusted trial balance. Use when the user has adjusted balances for a period and needs formal financial statements for it. Not for a P&L with commentary and runway straight from reconciled books, or for ratio analysis; see /bookkeeping-report or /finance-ratios.

name: accounting-trial-balance
description: Prepare an unadjusted trial balance from the general ledger and verify that total debits equal total credits, tracing any error. Use when the user has posted the ledger and wants to check the books balance before making period-end adjustments. Not for balances after adjusting entries; see /accounting-adjusted-balance.

name: accounting-variance
description: Compare actual results to budget, forecast or prior period line by line, with dollar and percentage variances and volume, price, mix or timing drivers. Use when actuals came in off plan and the user wants to know by how much and why. Not for a full performance review with KPI scorecard and reforecast; see /finance-review.

name: adorno

Use at the end of workflow:pr:review, workflow:review:requested and workflow:review:received, and in workflow:pr:open and workflow:pr:ship.

name: adorno-agent-chore-deps
description: agent:chore:deps — Update dependencies — outdated packages, advisories, lockfile drift. Use on a dependency bump request or a vulnerable or outdated package report; changes manifests and lockfile only.

name: adorno-agent-chore-repo
description: agent:chore:repo — Prepare a repo for agents — detect stack and commands, write AGENTS.md and CONSTRAINTS.md, propose the local/adorno.yaml entry. Use the first time a repo is used (workflow:repo:onboard).

name: adorno-agent-ci-debug
description: agent:ci:debug — Diagnose a red CI from the logs — classify the failure (flaky, infra, real failure) and name the agent that must fix it. Use as soon as a check fails on a PR or on the default branch.

name: adorno-agent-ci-fix
description: agent:ci:fix — Fix the CI pipeline itself — workflow file, job configuration, cache, matrix, pinned action, check script. Use when ci:debug classified a red check as a pipeline problem, not a code or test failure.

name: adorno-agent-core-analyst
description: agent:core:analyst — Analyzes a problem raised in a Slack conversation or a Notion document — what is asked, the context, the probable causes with evidence (code, logs, PRs, issues), what remains unknown, the proposed next step. Read-only. Use in workflow:slack:mentions, workflow:slack:watch and workflow:notion:assigned.

name: adorno-agent-core-intake
description: agent:core:intake — Frames a new code request and turns it into a spec with the permission level — either by discussing (discuss mode), or, when the request or its sources (clear prompt, Slack thread, Notion page, issue, already written plan) are enough, by writing it directly and asking only confirmation questions (confirm mode). Use at the start of any non-trivial request, before any code (workflow:spec:new).

name: adorno-agent-core-planner
description: agent:core:planner — Splits a validated spec into ordered vertical slices, each testable, and picks the family agent that will build each slice. Use after the router, before any implementation.

name: adorno-agent-core-router
description: agent:core:router — Picks the workflow pattern (none, sequential, parallel, evaluator-optimizer) from the validated spec and writes run-plan.yaml. Use right after a spec is validated.

name: adorno-agent-core-triage
description: agent:core:triage — Sorts the review feedback on a PR (category, area, specialist to consult, likely fixer) into triage.json. Never replies itself, agent:adorno rules and replies. Use in workflow:review:received.

name: adorno-agent-docs-write
description: agent:docs:write — Write or update documentation — README, guides, API reference, decision records — from the code and the change. Use when a feature, a behavior or a setting changed and its docs must follow.

name: adorno-agent-feat-api
description: agent:feat:api — API contracts — REST endpoints, methods, input and output schemas, contracts between modules. Use for a feat slice that creates or extends a public or internal interface.

name: adorno-agent-feat-back
description: agent:feat:back — Server-side features in any back-end stack — services, entry points (routes, RPC methods, handlers), jobs, database access. Use for a feat slice that touches server logic.

name: adorno-agent-feat-front
description: agent:feat:front — Interface-side features — components, pages, state, forms, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility. Use for a feat slice that touches the UI.

name: adorno-agent-fix-investigate
description: agent:fix:investigate — Investigate a bug — reproduce, isolate the cause, return a written diagnosis without changing anything. Use first on a reported bug, an issue or a red CI of unknown cause.

name: adorno-agent-fix-patch
description: agent:fix:patch — Fix a bug from a diagnosis or a review comment — red test that reproduces, then minimal fix. Use after fix:investigate, or on a review thread classified fix.

name: adorno-agent-fix-security
description: agent:fix:security — Fix a security finding — vulnerable code path, missing authorization, leaked secret or personal data, vulnerable dependency. Use on a finding from review:security or a security report, after the cause is understood.

name: adorno-agent-perf-front
description: agent:perf:front — Front-end performance — Core Web Vitals, bundle weight, re-renders, resource loading, interaction latency. Use on a slow page or component, a heavy bundle or a measured web-vitals regression.

name: adorno-agent-perf-mongodb
description: agent:perf:mongodb — MongoDB performance — slow queries and aggregations, missing or useless indexes, N+1, projections, volumes. Use on a slow query or screen where the database is suspected.

name: adorno-agent-perf-nodejs
description: agent:perf:nodejs — Node.js performance — CPU, memory and leaks, blocked event loop, sequential I/O, costly serialization. Use on a slow or resource-hungry Node.js service or job.

name: adorno-agent-refactor-simplify
description: agent:refactor:simplify — Simplify code without changing its behavior — dead code, duplication, needless abstractions, twisted conditions, and review nits. Use on a review comment classified nit or on code judged too complex.

name: adorno-agent-review-api
description: agent:review:api — API reviewer — endpoint and method contracts, input validation, error codes and formats, pagination, compatibility, public documentation. Called when a diff touches an interface, or to verify a review comment about an API.

name: adorno-agent-review-back
description: agent:review:back — Back-end reviewer — server logic in any stack, entry points (routes, RPC methods, handlers), jobs, errors, concurrency, server-side permissions, performance (unbounded reads, per-item I/O, blocking work in a request path, memory growth). Called when a diff touches the server, or to verify a review comment about the back end.

name: adorno-agent-review-code
description: agent:review:code — Code review on five axes (correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance) of a diff or a branch, findings in JSON for merging. Use before any PR is opened and on fix diffs.

name: adorno-agent-review-front
description: agent:review:front — Front-end reviewer — components, state, rendering, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, design system, web performance (Core Web Vitals, bundle weight, loading, interaction latency). Called when a diff touches the interface, or to verify a review comment about the front end.

name: adorno-agent-review-impact
description: agent:review:impact — Measures the real production impact of a merged PR — usage, errors, response time, throughput, resources, database, alerts — by comparing before and after its deployment across all available sources (logs, metrics, traces, errors, analytics, alert channels). Read-only, every number with its source. Use in workflow:pr:impact.

name: adorno-agent-review-mongodb
description: agent:review:mongodb — MongoDB reviewer — queries and aggregations, indexes, N+1, projections, bulk writes, migrations. Called when a diff contains queries or a migration, or to verify a review comment about the database.

name: adorno-agent-review-ponytail
description: agent:review:ponytail — Lean review of a diff — code that need not exist, a helper the repo already has, a dependency for a few lines, an unrequested abstraction, a `shortcut:` without limit or trigger. Use alongside review:code on every diff and on added dependencies; also audits a whole repo or a scope of it, read-only (workflow:repo:audit).

name: adorno-agent-review-security
description: agent:review:security — Security audit of a diff — OWASP Top 10, secrets, authentication and authorization, sensitive data, dependencies. Use whenever a diff touches user inputs, auth, data or dependencies.

name: adorno-agent-review-sql
description: agent:review:sql — SQL reviewer — relational queries through an ORM or raw SQL (ActiveRecord, Django ORM, database/sql, sqlx, GORM, knex…), N+1, indexes, unbounded reads, injection, migrations that lock a table. Called when a diff contains SQL, ORM queries or a migration on a relational database, or to verify a review comment about it.

name: adorno-agent-review-tests
description: agent:review:tests — Test review of a diff — coverage of risky paths, edge cases, errors, test readability. Use whenever logic changes.

name: adorno-agent-test-e2e
description: agent:test:e2e — End-to-end tests and browser QA with evidence — Playwright journeys, screenshots, video and trace attached to the report or the PR. Use to verify a front feature end to end, reproduce a UI bug or provide visual proof of a fix.

name: adorno-agent-test-unit
description: agent:test:unit — Write unit tests for existing logic or requested in review — nominal cases, limits, errors. Use on a review thread classified test or a gap listed by review:tests.

name: adorno-ci-red
description: Handles a red CI on a PR — diagnosis from the logs, a single rerun if flaky, otherwise a fix by the designated agent, committed and pushed without asking (workflow:pr:ship), the PR description updated if the scope moved. Use as soon as a check fails.

name: adorno-pr-open
description: Opens the PR of a ready branch, without asking — title and description in English following your template, in your voice, reviewers from the registry. Ready for review when the review loop of workflow:pr:ship left nothing 🔴 or 🟠, draft otherwise. Default pr_skill of workflow:pr:ship.

name: adorno-pr-review
description: Reviews a colleague's PR in a dedicated workspace — specialized reviewers chosen by the touched code areas (front, back, mongodb, api, security…), in parallel, then your agent who rechecks, slices and writes. By default, a pending review that you reread and submit yourself.

name: adorno-pr-ship
description: Ends every workflow that touched code — commit (the repo's commit_skill), review and fix until no 🔴 or 🟠 is left and the change meets the request, its proof attached (test output, screenshots and videos of what a user sees), then the PR (the repo's pr_skill) opened ready for review, or pushed and updated when it is already open. No confirmation and no permission prompt, within the run's level. Last step of feature:build, issue:fix, ci:red, review:received and repo:onboard.

name: adorno-pr-status
description: Status of all your open PRs (or those of one repo) — review, CI, unresolved threads, and what blocks each one. Read-only.

name: adorno-pr-watch
description: Accompanies an open PR until it is ready to merge — loops on red CI and new review threads, with a cap. The merge stays yours.

name: adorno-profile-learn
description: Evolve your profile and your voice — reviews the points noted by adorno-learn during work (tech, product logic, code logic, method, writing), shows you each with its evidence and the proposed sentence in the right file, and writes only what you validate, in your personal layer. name: adorno-repo-audit

name: adorno-repo-onboard

name: adorno-review-received

name: adorno-review-requested

description: BBC — design the black boxes of a new project, or of a new part of one, from the requirements, with the user, before any code ({@tasks}/bbc/): the black boxes by responsibility, their contracts, dependencies and flows, the decisions of the architecture. No code is read. The diagram is approved before the details; then /dev:bbc-review, and back here with its findings until the user approves the map. name: bbc-audit
description: BBC — check whether the code reflects the analysis: each black box's code in its namespace, its contract in the Core as the map writes it, the dependencies only through the Core and only those on the map, the decisions of the map kept. It writes a report, and the findings are fixed by one feature. Use when the roadmap reaches the audit, after BBs were built or changed, or the user says bbc audit, il codice rispecchia la mappa, controlla il codice contro la BBC.

name: bbc-core
description: BBC — plan the Core of the contracts, the first step of the roadmap; on a project with no code yet it is the project's start — the profile, the skeleton, then the Core. Every contract of the map written in the project's Core — the abstract concepts of the whole system, each BB's interfaces and the types they exchange under the BB's namespace — with its fake and its contract tests, so that every BB can then be developed in parallel against it. A TDDAB plan, reviewed, then it STOPS and the user triggers /dev:j-cvm-exec-plan. Use when the roadmap's first step is due, or the user says bbc core, s…

name: bbc-debug
description: BBC — fix a bug that crosses several black boxes. The bug path of /dev:j-bug — LISTEN, DIAGNOSE with Protocol D, PLAN — with ISOLATE done on the map, the BBs' tests run leaves first, then the integration points; then STOPS, the user triggers /dev:j-cvm-exec-plan. Use when a failure spans several BBs and cannot be placed, or the user says bbc debug.

name: bbc-e2e
description: BBC — plan the end-to-end tests of the map's flows: every flow that crosses the black boxes, through the real transport and the real storage, at the level the project has (the API, the user interface). A TDDAB plan, reviewed and ready for /dev:j-cvm-exec-plan. Use when the user says bbc e2e, test dei flussi, or /dev:bbc-integrate pointed here.

name: bbc-integrate
description: BBC — integrate black boxes after one of them changed its contract or they were built apart. Every call between them is checked on both sides of the contract, and a TDDAB plan proves them wired together, real BB with real BB; the map's integration points are updated. Use when the roadmap says built BBs meet, after /dev:bbc-plan changed a contract, or when the user says bbc integrate, integra i BB, test tra i BB.

name: bbc-plan
description: BBC — plan the development of one black box as a feature. From the BB's definition in the map — its responsibility, its contract, its dependencies — the phases of /dev:j-new-feature scoped to the BB write a TDDAB plan, the cases of the contract as the tests and the implementation behind it, the other BBs as the fakes of the Core, the Core's contract tests run against the real implementation; the plan is reviewed, then it STOPS and the user triggers /dev:j-cvm-exec-plan. Use when the user says bbc plan, sviluppa il BB, pianifica il BB, or names a black box of the roadmap to build.

name: bbc-refactor
description: BBC — change a black box of the map — its responsibility, its contract, a split or a merge, a decision — and then the code that follows it: the phases of a feature up to a reviewed plan, the map changed and approved first. Use when the user says bbc refactor, cambia il BB, sposta la responsabilità, dividi o unisci i BB, or /dev:bbc-audit sent a finding of the map here.

name: bbc-review
description: BBC — review the analysis: the black-box map against the requirements and the method — the boundaries, the contracts, the connections, the logic of the flows, the requirements and the decisions — with no code read; write what is wrong with where and why, and send it back to /dev:bbc-analyze, until the user approves the map; then propose the roadmap of the development — the Core of the contracts, the BBs (in parallel when the user wants), the integrations, the flows, the audit of the code — approved by the user and written in the map. Use after /dev:bbc-analyze, before working on the BBs, or w…

Investiga (codigo + web), verifica impacto cross-flow, propone 2-3 opciones y construye el plan INCREMENTALMENTE: cada increment pasa su revision de diseno antes de escribirse al MD. Escala la ceremonia al tamano (trivial->directo, task->ligero, grande->deep-plan). TRIGGER — el usuario describe QUE quiere lograr (una historia/necesidad), no una solucion ya hecha. NOTA: se llama bossdream-plan (NO plan) para no colisionar con el Plan Mode NATIVO de Claude Code.

TRIGGER — el usuario quiere iniciar la documentacion de negocio de una iniciativa nueva, antes de poder correr /bossdream-validate o /bossdream-plan sobre ella.

name: bossdream-report

TRIGGER — el usuario quiere un resumen humano del proyecto activo, sin que eso agregue documentos al gate de Document Validation.

TRIGGER — el usuario quiere retomar un proyecto que otro dev ya documento, cambiar de proyecto para apoyar en otro, o volver al modo normal (bossdream-plan/bossdream-implement sin gobernanza de proyecto) para una tarea suelta.

TRIGGER — proceso unico y puntual: el usuario lo invoca cuando quiere auditar/actualizar el catalogo completo de skills del proyecto, sin instruccion adicional del usuario sobre que explorar.

TRIGGER — el usuario edito documentos manualmente y quiere que el sistema se entere, o describe alcance nuevo que todavia no esta escrito en requirements.md.

name: cpv-agent
description: Direct free-form entry to the general-purpose CPV worker. name: cpv-batch-caching-audit
description: Fan out cpv-cache-optimizer-agent across every plugin in a marketplace, a list of plugins, or a single plugin. Accepts local paths and GitHub URLs. One cpv-cache-optimizer-agent per plugin running in batch_audit mode (read-only — Phase 1 of the cache pipeline). Detects the seven prompt-cache-invalidation patterns (CA-01..CA-07) per plugin without applying fixes. Parallel main-session dispatch (default 8, cap 16).

name: cpv-batch-caching-optimize
description: Fan out cpv-cache-optimizer-agent across every plugin in a marketplace, a list of plugins, or a single plugin and APPLY the cache-invalidation fixes (CA-01..CA-07). Accepts local paths and GitHub URLs. One cpv-cache-optimizer-agent per plugin in batch_fix mode (Phase 1 audit + Phase 2 fix + Phase 3 re-validate; Phase 4 broader refactor SKIPPED in batch mode to avoid per-plugin user prompts). Parallel main-session dispatch (default 8, cap 16).

name: cpv-batch-fix
description: Parallel fix for one OR many plugins. Single-plugin inputs run the existing per-shard protocol (one cpv-plugin-fixer-agent per shard of findings). Marketplace / list / URL inputs run a per-plugin fan-out (one cpv-plugin-fixer-agent per plugin; each fixer may internally shard its own findings). Accepts local paths, GitHub URLs, marketplace URLs/folders, comma-separated lists, and @listfile shapes. Default 8 parallel agents per main-session message, cap 16. Each agent starts with a fresh context window (size determined by `cpv-plugin-fixer-agent.model`).

name: cpv-batch-full-scan-and-fix
description: Maximum-coverage same-turn scan + fix. One cpv-plugin-fixer-agent per plugin reads each source file ONCE and runs validate + security + caching audit + caching optimize + verify-FPs + fix — all inline. Each per-file scan triggers every applicable checker; confirmed-real findings are fixed; confirmed-FPs are skipped. Cuts per-plugin token cost ~5× vs running the four separate batch skills sequentially. Default 8 parallel agents per main-session message, cap 16.

name: cpv-batch-scope-diagnose
description: Read-only diagnostic across a fleet of project folders. One cpv-doctor-agent per project diagnoses the requested scope — user (~/.claude/), project (<project>/.claude/), local (<project>/.claude/settings.local.json), or full (all three + cross-scope conflict checker). LOCAL paths only — URL inputs are CRITICAL errors because the doctor needs ~/.claude/ filesystem access. Default 8 parallel agents per main-session message, cap 16.

name: cpv-batch-scope-diagnose-and-fix
description: Same-turn diagnose + fix across a fleet of project folders. One cpv-doctor-agent per project scans the requested scope + verifies findings + applies obvious fixes inline (NIT and CRITICAL auto; MAJOR / MINOR auto when the recipe is safe). LOCAL paths only — URL inputs are CRITICAL errors. Default 8 parallel agents per main-session message, cap 16.

name: cpv-batch-scope-fix
description: Apply fixes for scope-aware doctor findings across a fleet of project folders. One cpv-doctor-agent per project in batch_scope_fix mode handles the requested scope (user / project / local / full). LOCAL paths only — URL inputs are CRITICAL errors. Default 8 parallel agents per main-session message, cap 16.

name: cpv-batch-security-audit
description: Fan out security-only validation across every plugin in a marketplace, a list of plugins, or a single plugin. Accepts local paths and GitHub URLs. One cpv-plugin-validator-agent agent per plugin (mode batch_security_audit) running only the security checker — five external scanners (cc-audit, tirith, trufflehog, semgrep, Cisco AI Defense skill-scanner) plus the in-process AI/security rule pack. Parallel main-session dispatch (default 8 at a time, cap 16).

name: cpv-batch-validate
description: Fan out cpv-plugin-validator-agent agents across every plugin in a marketplace, a list of plugins, or a single plugin. Accepts local paths and GitHub URLs. One validator agent per plugin, dispatched in parallel from a single main-session message (default 8 at a time, cap 16). Returns one consolidated severity table covering every scanned plugin.

name: cpv-batch-validate-and-fix
description: Same-turn validate-and-fix across a marketplace / list / single plugin. One cpv-plugin-fixer-agent per plugin scans + verifies false positives + fixes ALL findings in the same turn — each source file is READ ONCE, not the three times the separate validate → fix → re-validate cycle requires. Cuts per-plugin token cost ~3×. Default 8 parallel agents per main-session message, cap 16.

name: hx-doc
description: 1. 执行 `hx-doc context <feature-or-source>`，读取需求来源、模板和现有文档事实；若返回 `feature` 与入参不同，以返回值为准。 2. 在 workspace 多项目目录中扫描可能受影响的服务，确认协调层、执行服务和关联服务。 3. 生成或续接 `docs/requirement/{feature}.md`，再执行 `hx-doc validate <feature>`。 4. 校验失败时只修正文档本身。

name: hx-go
description: 1. 执行 `hx-go next <feature>`，读取当前 step 的 `toolScript`、`preHooks`、`postHooks`。 2. 按顺序执行：读取 `preHooks` → 运行 `toolScript` → 读取 `postHooks`。 3. 遇到 `checkpoint.message` 时启动子 agent 评审，按结论继续或重跑当前 step。 4. 若 `audit.stopReason` 非空，停止并说明预算命中的 step、原因和下一步。 5. 重复直到 `allDone` 或明确阻断。

name: hx-init
description: 1. 执行 `hx-init`，完成当前目录或指定目录的初始化。

name: hx-mr
description: 1. 先执行 `git status --porcelain`；存在未提交修改时，先按团队规范提交当前修改。 2. 执行 `git push origin <current-branch>`，确保远端分支与本地一致；push 失败则终止。 3. 基于需求文档、计划/进度和已提交变更生成 MR 标题与描述，再创建 MR。 4. MR 创建成功后执行 `hx-mr archive <feature>`；创建失败不归档。

name: hx-plan
description: 1. 执行 `hx-plan context <feature>`，读取需求文档、计划模板和进度文件。 2. 生成或续接 `planDoc`，让运行时初始化或校验 `progressFile`。

name: hx-reset
description: 1. 执行 `hx-reset <feature> [plan|doc|code]`，删除或回退目标 feature 的对应产物。 2. 根据脚本返回的结果确认重置范围；未指定参数时按同时重置 `code`、`plan` 和 `doc` 处理。

name: hx-review
description: 1. 执行 `hx-review [<feature>]`，读取评审结果。 2. 若 `qa.needsAiReview` 为真，根据 `qa.context` 分析项目并配置 gates，再重新执行。 3. 若 `review.needsAiReview` 为真，根据 `review.context` 做 verifier 评审，报告问题、风险和未覆盖项。 4. 未通过时停止，输出结论和问题。

name: hx-run
description: 1. 执行 `hx-run next <feature>`，读取当前批次任务。 2. 实现当前批次任务： - 脚本按依赖图计算批次，返回 `parallel: true` 时并行实现批次内所有 task，`parallel: false` 时顺序实现 - 每个 task 以 `tasksContext[].execution.root` 为工作目录执行，质量门命令使用 `execution.gates` 3. 先检查 `audit.stopReason` 和 task 的 `audit.riskClass`；预算耗尽时停止，高风险变更必须保留证据。 4. 按 `tasksContext[].doneCriteria` 校验完成证据：任务契约满足、验证命令通过、变更范围可解释。 5. 满足后通过 `hx-progress done <progressFile> <taskId> --outp

name: hx-server
description: 1. 执行 `hx-server [<target>]`，读取已记录的服务启动方式。 2. 若返回已记录服务，用后台 shell 在其 `cwd` 执行 `command`，观察日志直到出现监听地址或明确失败。 3. 若记录缺失或启动失败，分析项目结构、README、脚本、入口文件和环境示例，继续尝试直到找到可成功启动的命令。 4. 启动成功后执行 `hx-server save <id> --cwd <cwd> --command <command> --type <type> [--url <url>]` 写回记录。 5. 输出服务类型、执行目录、命令和访问地址；无法启动时说明具体阻断。

name: hx-status
description: 1. 执行 `hx-status [<feature>]`，读取指定或全部 feature 的进度摘要事实。 2. 根据脚本返回的状态展示当前阶段、剩余任务和推荐动作。

name: hx-test
description: 1. 执行 `hx-test <feature>`，读取 `test.context`。 2. 若 `test.needsSubagent` 为真，启动干净上下文的子 agent，并把 `test.context` 作为唯一任务上下文交给它。 3. 子 agent 必须根据目标类型做真实端到端验证：前端启动浏览器操作页面，服务端启动服务后真实调用接口并检查请求与返回。 4. 子 agent 输出必须区分已验证、失败、未覆盖、复现步骤和证据。 5. 若发现错误，主 agent 按子 agent 给出的复现与日志修复，再重新执行 `hx test <feature>`。 6. 测试通过后继续 `hx mr <feature>`。

Zero arguments needed. --loop (or orchestration.next_execution "loop" in config.json) makes the execute/verify states run the bounded ralph loop instead of single steps.

name: jdi-plan

name: jdi-remove-phase

name: jdi-ship

name: jdi-status

name: jdi-verify

description: Improve test quality by analyzing and strengthening weak, brittle, or poorly-written tests

name: lisa:ingest
description: Ingest source material into the LLM Wiki. With an argument (URL, file path, or prompt) ingest that one source; with no argument run a full ingest across every enabled non-external-write source. Routes to the right connector and runs the ordered pipeline (source note → synthesis → index → log → verify → state → commit/PR).

name: lisa:intake
description: Vendor-agnostic batch scanner for Ready queues. Notion PRD database URL → finds Status=Ready PRDs and runs lisa-plan per item. Confluence space or parent-page URL → finds prd-ready PRDs and runs lisa-plan per item. Linear workspace or team URL → finds prd-ready Linear projects and runs lisa-plan per item. GitHub repo URL or org/repo token → finds prd-ready GitHub issues and runs lisa-plan per item (PRD-source mode), or finds status:ready issues and runs lisa-implement per item when tracker=github (build-queue mode). JIRA project key or JQL → finds Ready tickets and runs lisa-implement per ite…

name: lisa:intake-explain
description: Inspect one PRD or build item, explain how Lisa classifies it right now, and report the exact intake or repair gate affecting it. Read-only by default.

name: lisa:learnings:audit
description: Run one gardener cycle over this project's knowledge surfaces (the learnings ladder, PRD #1729): inventory ledger/rules/skills/wiki/mechanical controls, gather evidence, classify via the ladder router, and file human-gated tracker tickets — per-item PROMOTE/DEMOTE tickets, one CONFIRM/RETIRE batch ticket per run, upstream Lisa issues for upstream-scoped patterns. Everything is human-gated; the run only files marker-deduped tickets. Terminal states: nothing-needed | candidates-proposed | blocked.

name: lisa:lint
description: Health-check the LLM Wiki: orphan pages, contradictions, stale claims, broken internal links, missing index/log coverage, structure violations, and secret/tenant leaks. Read-only — reports findings, does not fix them.

name: lisa:migrate
description: Migrate an existing hand-rolled wiki onto the lisa-wiki kernel — phased and compatibility-first, with a strict no-loss guarantee (renaming is fine; losing functionality or data is not). Ends by running /doctor.

name: lisa:monitor
description: Monitor application health AND audit observability completeness for the current repo, then file build-ready tickets for anomalies and instrumentation gaps. Health/logs/errors/performance via the stack ops-specialist or stack-agnostic base probing; repo-scoped, idempotent, capped; files by default, --dry-run previews.

name: lisa:onboard-me
description: Onboard a user to the project via its LLM Wiki: interview them about themselves in relation to the project, then give a guided tour and sample questions. Read-mostly by default (session-local); --save-memory persists the capture to project-scoped memory only. No PRs, no PII written into the wiki, never global memory.

name: lisa:parity-code-review
description: Lisa-native code review of the current git diff — correctness bugs, security issues, and obvious defects, reported as severity-ranked findings with file:line references. Vendor-neutral cross-agent equivalent of the upstream code-review command.

name: lisa:parity-code-simplifier
description: Behavior-preserving simplification of recently-changed code — dedup, reuse, readability, and dead-code removal, quality only (never a bug hunt). Vendor-neutral cross-agent equivalent of the upstream code-simplifier agent.

name: lisa:parity-coderabbit
description: Thorough PR-style review of the full diff — bugs, security, performance, and maintainability — with concrete fixes and a structured summary. An independent Lisa-native review (does NOT call CodeRabbit's service); vendor-neutral cross-agent equivalent of the upstream coderabbit plugin.

name: lisa:parity-safety-net-rules
description: View, set, and verify the custom guard rules enforced by Lisa's safety-net PreToolUse Bash hook — the cross-agent equivalent of the upstream safety-net plugin's set/verify-custom-rules skills.

name: lisa:parity-sentry-sdk-setup
description: Install and configure the Sentry SDK for a project — detect the framework, add the right @sentry/<framework> package, init the client, wire the DSN via env, enable error + performance monitoring, and set up source maps. One consolidated skill covering react, nextjs, node, nestjs, python, react-native, and more.

name: lisa:parity-sentry-seer
description: AI debugging — given an error, stack trace, or failing test, analyze it, form ranked hypotheses, locate the root cause in the codebase with file:line evidence, and propose a minimal fix. Lisa-native reimplementation of Sentry's seer workflow.

name: lisa:parity-skill-creator
description: Author a new Lisa skill end-to-end — scaffold the SKILL.md frontmatter, write the pass-through command, follow hyphen naming and placement under plugins/src, and rebuild plugins. Lisa-native equivalent of the upstream skill-creator plugin.

name: lisa:persist-learning
description: Route a candidate learning through the hostile-default learning-judge gate and act on the verdict: leave a dropped-with-reason note on the triggering issue (drop), file the upstream Lisa ticket automatically with marker dedupe, evidence, and a per-run cap (lisa-upstream), or persist a durable learning via a confidence-routed PR that touches only the learnings surface — auto-merge on for high confidence, auto-merge off plus the learning:needs-triage label for low confidence. Idempotent via marker dedupe.

name: lisa:plan
description: Plan work from a single PRD or specification. Decomposes into ordered work items in the configured tracker (JIRA, GitHub Issues, or Linear per .lisa.config.json). Source can be a Notion / Confluence / Linear / GitHub Issue URL, a JIRA epic key, a markdown file, or a free-form description. For batch scanning of all Ready PRDs in a queue, use /lisa:intake instead.

name: lisa:plugin-sync-explain
description: Explain plugin source/generated drift and marketplace registration gaps without modifying the working tree.

name: lisa:product-walkthrough
description: Walk through the live product via a real browser (Playwright MCP) to ground PRD evaluation or ticket creation in what exists today. Captures current behavior, design-vs-product divergence, reuse candidates, and behavioral surprises.

name: lisa:product-walkthrough
description: Walk through the live product via a real browser controlled interactively through any capable backend to ground PRD evaluation or ticket creation in what exists today. Captures current behavior, design-vs-product divergence, reuse candidates, and behavioral surprises.

name: lisa:project-ideation
description: Generate persona-grounded, verifiable product ideas for the host project, then create PRDs for the selected build-ready ideas via lisa-research. First derives the personas the project actually serves (from its docs, code, data model, and releases — never invented), ideates per persona, and gates each idea on an obtainable data/source path and an empirical verification plan. Creates one PRD by default (top-ranked idea); max_prds widens the batch. prd_ready=true creates them prd-ready for auto-pickup by lisa-intake; default is draft for human review.

name: lisa:pull-request:review
description: Address and resolve PR review comments (human + bot): implement valid feedback, reply to invalid, resolve every thread.

name: lisa:query
description: Answer a question from the LLM Wiki with citations. Reads the index, drills into relevant pages, and synthesizes a cited answer. Read-only by default; files new synthesis back only when explicitly asked.

name: lisa:queue-status
description: Inspect the current project's PRD and build queues, summarize lifecycle counts, and surface actionable queue-health signals without mutating work.

name: lisa:repair-intake
description: Repair counterpart to /lisa:intake. Vendor-agnostic batch scanner that finds stuck or half-closed work — items in `blocked`, stalled in an in-progress role (build `claimed`, PRD `in_review`), terminal-labeled items still natively open, rollups whose children are all terminal, GitHub PRDs missing native child links, and GitHub issues missing Lisa lifecycle labels — across the same queues /lisa:intake serves. Repairs every actionable candidate inside the `max_candidates` cap: resumes stalled work in place (diagnosing PR/deploy state first; unmergeable PRs or failed deploys get a build-ready fix…

name: lisa:research
description: Research a problem space and create a PRD in the configured PRD source. Investigates the codebase, defines user flows, assesses technical feasibility, synthesizes the spec, then creates it in the source (Notion / Confluence / GitHub / Linear) via lisa-prd-source-write — no loose document. prd_ready=true creates it prd-ready for auto-pickup by lisa-intake; default is draft for the Plan flow / human review.

name: lisa:review:local

name: lisa:rework-triage

name: lisa:session-manager

Dispatches Ready work items to fresh background worker sessions and relays their questions over the project's Telegram bot when one is configured (Telegram is optional). Claude Code only; configure it with /lisa:setup:session-manager.

name: lisa:setup
description: Scaffold, repair, verify, or upgrade the project's LLM Wiki from its config. Asks the wiki's purpose and README mode, renders the contract snapshot, scaffolds the canonical folders, and seeds the staff roster. Idempotent and non-destructive.

name: lisa:setup-automations
description: Set up the recurring LLM Wiki ingest automation on the local workstation using the runtime's native scheduler (Codex automations / Claude /schedule): wiki-ingest, a full /lisa-wiki:ingest cycle, once a day by default (override with cadence). A declarative spec — it states what to schedule and how often; the runtime's native automation mechanism does the creating. Named lisa-wiki-auto-<project>-* so it never collides with the base /lisa:setup-automations set. The wiki counterpart of /lisa:setup-automations, separate because the wiki plugin is standalone.

name: lisa:setup-openclaw
description: Set up OpenClaw as the chat-surface runtime for this project's staff. Verifies the openclaw CLI, ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, a secret provider, and required gateway capabilities, then writes a lean `openclaw` section to .lisa.config.json. Run before connect-staff / connect-repo-topic.

name: lisa:setup-remote-aws
description: Install Lisa's vendor-neutral AWS CLI bootstrap and platform adapters for remote coding environments.

name: lisa:setup:atlassian
description: Set up Atlassian (cloudId + acli profile) for this project. Writes the `atlassian` section of `.lisa.config.json` and enables the Atlassian MCP and/or installs acli as needed. Prerequisite for /lisa:setup:jira and /lisa:setup:confluence.

name: lisa:setup:aws
description: Provision the dev/staging/production/shared AWS accounts this CDK project deploys into via the @codyswann/aws-soc2-setup CLI (Organizations, Control Tower, IAM Identity Center, SOC 2 controls), then wire them in end-to-end: SSO profiles, cdk bootstrap with pipeline trust, PLACEHOLDER account IDs in config/environments.ts, AWS_ACCOUNT_ID_* GitHub secrets, and the .lisa.config.json account map. Idempotent; console-only prerequisites (root MFA, Identity Center, landing zone) surface as a human checklist instead of being automated.

name: lisa:setup:confluence
description: Set up Confluence as the PRD source for this project. Writes the `confluence` section of `.lisa.config.json` (spaceKey and/or parentPageId) and offers to set top-level `source: "confluence"`. Depends on /lisa:setup:atlassian.

name: lisa:setup:github
description: Set up GitHub Issues as the tracker and/or PRD source for this project. Verifies the gh CLI, resolves org/repo, scaffolds the `status:*` (build) and/or `prd-*` (PRD) label namespaces, writes the `github` section of `.lisa.config.json`, and can document optional GitHub ProjectV2 coordination before offering top-level `tracker: "github"` / `source: "github"`. No /lisa:setup:atlassian prerequisite.

name: lisa:setup:github-repo
description: Apply Lisa's GitHub repository governance baseline: merge-only settings with auto-merge and delete-branch-on-merge, branch + tag rulesets (CodeRabbit/GitGuardian/Quality Checks gates, prevent delete, protect tags), a CI deploy key + DEPLOY_KEY secret, and optional deployment environments with human-approval gates from .lisa.config.json github.environments. Idempotent; per-repo overrides via .lisa.config.json github.settings.

name: lisa:setup:github-repo
description: Apply Lisa's GitHub repository governance baseline: merge-only settings with auto-merge and delete-branch-on-merge, branch + tag rulesets (CodeRabbit/GitGuardian/Quality Checks gates, prevent delete, protect tags), and a CI deploy key + DEPLOY_KEY secret. Idempotent; per-repo overrides via .lisa.config.json github.settings.

name: lisa:setup:jira
description: Set up JIRA as the tracker for this project. Writes `jira.project` and offers to set top-level `tracker: "jira"` in `.lisa.config.json`. Depends on /lisa:setup:atlassian (needs cloudId).

name: lisa:setup:linear
description: Set up Linear as the tracker and/or PRD source for this project. Verifies Linear access (MCP OAuth or a personal API key in keychain), resolves the workspace slug and team key, scaffolds the `status:*` issue-label (build) and/or `prd-*` project-label (PRD) namespaces, writes the `linear` section of `.lisa.config.json`, and offers to set top-level `tracker: "linear"` / `source: "linear"`. No /lisa:setup:atlassian prerequisite.

name: lisa:setup:linear
description: Set up Linear as the tracker and/or PRD source for this project. Verifies Linear access (MCP OAuth or a personal API key in keychain), resolves the workspace slug and team key, scaffolds the build-queue workflow states (`linear.workflow`) and/or `prd-*` project-label (PRD) namespaces, writes the `linear` section of `.lisa.config.json`, and offers to set top-level `tracker: "linear"` / `source: "linear"`. No /lisa:setup:atlassian prerequisite.

name: lisa:setup:local-env
description: Bring this machine in line with the toolchain the project declares. Reports every tool in remoteEnv.tools that is missing, outdated, or unpinned for this platform, and installs the missing ones into ~/.local/bin from the same pinned, checksummed entries the remote surfaces use — but only when asked with --install-tools. A newer tool already on PATH is left alone.

name: lisa:setup:notion
description: Set up Notion as the PRD source for this project. Walks the user through creating a workspace-scoped internal-integration token, sharing the PRD database with it, and stores the token in OS keychain. Writes `notion.workspaceId`, `notion.prdDatabaseId`, and `notion.values` into `.lisa.config.json`. Offers to set top-level `source: "notion"`.

name: lisa:setup:remote-env
description: Provision and verify a remote execution environment for this project — Codex Cloud today. Generates the repository-owned setup script that installs the declared toolchain, materializes secrets through lisa-secrets-access, and runs the project's own hook. Provisions by API where one exists, by driving the vendor console where one does not, and by emitting exact config otherwise, then proves the result with the same read-back regardless of tier. Run this before dispatching work with executionEnv.

name: lisa:setup:session-manager
description: Set up the local session manager for this project: write the sessionManager config block, optionally set up Telegram notifications (store the project's own bot token in its secrets provider, migrating any plaintext token file, check the plugin scope, walk through pairing; skipped with no channel, the default), seed the runbook, start the manager in tmux, and run doctor's session-manager check.

name: lisa:setup:sonar
description: Wire the official SonarQube plugin + MCP into this project across every supported coding agent. Installs/updates the SonarQube CLI, authenticates (browser login on a dev machine, or SONARQUBE_CLI_TOKEN headless), selects the Test Manager target, runs `sonar integrate <agent>` for each supported agent, and writes only non-secret policy to `.lisa.config.json`. Does not touch the separate CI SonarCloud scan gate.

description: Scaffold, repair, verify, or upgrade the project's LLM Wiki from its config. Alias for lisa-wiki setup in the Lisa setup command family.

name: lisa:setup:workstation
description: Prepare this machine — or a throwaway container — to run coding agents, before any repository exists. Detects which of Lisa's supported agents are already installed, asks which credential manager the machine uses (or none), and installs only what is missing, each by its vendor's own preferred method. Idempotent and headless; --print-dockerfile emits a spin-up/spin-down environment. Nothing is installed without --install.

A declarative spec — it states which automation to remove; the runtime's native mechanism does the removing. Removes only this project's wiki automation, never the base set or other projects'.

name: lisa:track

name: lisa:validate-tracker-mapping

Read-only by default; repairs the config to canonical live names with repair=true. Audits the current repo or sweeps many via projects=/workspaces=.

name: lisa:verify
description: Ship and verify code. Commits, opens PR, handles review loop, merges, monitors deploy, and runs remote verification in target environment. Folds in /ship.

name: lisa:verify-prd
description: Initiative-level PRD acceptance gate. Reads a shipped PRD and its generated child work, confirms all generated top-level work is terminal, then runs spec-conformance against the PRD plus empirical verification of the shipped surface. On a CONFORMS verdict with all checks passing it transitions the PRD shipped → verified with evidence; on a conformance miss (PARTIAL/DIVERGES) or any failing empirical check it re-opens the PRD shipped → ticketed (never blocked), creates build-ready fix tickets for the gaps, and posts a failure report — the fix tickets auto-build, the PRD re-ships, and it re-ver…

name: lisa:verify-workflow-change

name: lisa:wiki:install
description: Enable the LLM Wiki kernel (lisa-wiki plugin) in this project so its setup skill becomes discoverable. Edits .claude/settings.json to enable lisa-wiki@lisa and confirm the CodySwannGT/lisa marketplace, then verifies the Codex overlay (.codex/skills/lisa) already carries the wiki kernel. Does NOT scaffold the wiki itself — after install, reload the runtime and run /setup:wiki (Claude) or $lisa-wiki-setup (Codex).

name: om-auto-continue-pr

Use plain om-auto-continue-pr for simple runs.

name: om-auto-create-pr

Drafts a Progress-tracked execution plan, commits on a fresh worktree branch, implements phase-by-phase, runs the configured validation gate, applies pipeline labels. Long plans hand off to om-auto-create-pr-loop automatically. Resumable via om-auto-continue-pr.

name: om-auto-create-pr-loop

Resumable via om-auto-continue-pr-loop. Use plain om-auto-create-pr for small fixes.

name: om-auto-fix-issue
description: Fix or implement a tracker issue end to end from a single command — takes an issue id or a plain problem description (filed first via om-prepare-issue), classifies, then drives the bug autofix chain (om-verify-in-repo, om-root-cause, om-fix, om-open-pr, om-auto-review-pr, om-auto-qa-pr for UI fixes) or the feature route (spec via om-auto-write-spec, built via om-auto-implement-spec). Isolated worktree, claim protocol, clean stops. Use for \"fix issue 123\" or a pasted problem description.

name: om-auto-fix-pr
description: Drive an open PR to merge-ready from its number — merges the latest base, then loops review-autofix (om-auto-review-pr), built-in CI stabilization, and UI verification (om-auto-qa-pr) until approvable, green, and QA-evidenced. A --ci-only mode drives just CI green on a PR or a plain branch. Files follow-up issues for nits, normalizes labels, hands off to om-approve-merge-pr — never merges itself. Use for \"get PR 123 merge-ready\".

name: om-auto-implement-spec

A spec PR stays design-only — implementation ships on its own PR referencing it. Delegates to om-auto-create-pr (om-auto-continue-pr for an existing implementation PR), then runs the review loop and UI verification with screenshots. Use for \"implement the spec X\", \"build spec from issue 123\".
